title: Basic-open sections compare a quasi-coherent complex with its K-injective resolution
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $g\in A$, and $F,J$ integer-indexed complexes of module sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume every $F^n$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], $J$ is K-injective, and $i:F\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Then the map of $A$-module complexes $\Gamma(D(g),i)$, with sections and the $A$-action as in [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total], is a quasi-isomorphism. No boundedness or quasi-coherence of the terms of $J$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08C2, one-element affine cover; Tags 08BS and 08D2. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08C2 and /08D2; local TeX absent.

proof.text: Restrict F,J,i to D(g) with overFunctor and then the module equivalence overEquiv. Restriction and equivalence are exact, hence preserve the quasi-isomorphism; open restriction preserves K-injectivity, and the equivalence preserves it by the exact-adjoint criterion. Transport quasi-coherence through overFunctorEquiv and the quasi-coherent object property. D(g) is affine, including the empty case.

Apply qcoh_complex_alternating_cech_derived_sections to the singleton cover by top on the restricted affine scheme. Obtain an invertible comparison beta, and apply its defining equation to the actual restricted resolution i. The derived image of i and the K-injective computation isomorphism are invertible. The singleton augmentation at J is invertible by the singleton lemma. Thus the equation proves that Q of the Cech total map is invertible.

Apply naturality of the singleton augmentation to i. Both its F and J components are isomorphisms; the preceding step makes Q of the total map an isomorphism. Cancel the augmentation at J to deduce that Q of the global-section map is an isomorphism, hence that the global-section map is a quasi-isomorphism.
Use the restriction comparison equivalence to reflect the quasi-isomorphism of restricted global sections to the affineOpenSections A-module map in the unchanged conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tags 08C2 and 08BS, with Perfect Tag 08D2; implementation by the existing canonical comparison equation, explicit singleton augmentation isomorphism, and scalar-restriction comparison.

theorem principalOpenSections_resolution_quasiIso
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (g : A)
    (F J : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, (F.X n).IsQuasicoherent)

      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map i)
